products.summary: A 2.8 lb five-section tripod that folds to about 15.5 in, the diameter of a water bottle, and still reaches 51.25 in with the center column down. cons: Ball head has one adjustment ring and no separate pan; owners add a pan clamp for panoramas

Peak Design Travel Tripod (Carbon Fiber).date: a year ago (as of Oct 2026 scrape)
Peak Design Travel Tripod (Carbon Fiber).text: We photograph the Northern Lights in Fairbanks, Alaska — often in -40° to -50°F temperatures, for hours at a time, and completely in the dark.
The small form factor and light weight design make it almost unnoticeable while I'm carrying it in my backpack.
The only real downside that I have experienced with the PD head is that its not great for panning.
Suggestions for improvement: the soft case is a bit tight at the top and hard to close.
I sadly endured the issue that others have, and that's with the latch/leg lock. It snapped. It's cheap casted metal.

Peak Design Travel Tripod (Carbon Fiber).who: Michael, B&H (promotion-collected, not counted in owners.read)
Peak Design Travel Tripod (Carbon Fiber).text: My only minor complaint is the lack of a built-in panning function for the ball head.
Great device. well engineered. Thoughtful design. Expensive but. worth it. Light. Better for the human back
It's small and something I don't have to ask myself if I should bring it or not because of it's size and weight!

Peak Design Travel Tripod (Aluminum).text: I absolutely love the portability as I take it with me on all my hikes and camping trips.

this tripod is not great in the wind. There are only two notches for different leg widths and the first is very narrow, while the second is super wide and will only get the camera about 8" off the ground. I have had my camera blow over in the wind.
I have this stowed in its bag attached to my pack with carabiners and I couldn't be happier.
It is most often paired with a heavy and bulky Canon 6D SLR + 70-200mm and is rock-solid.
The tripod legs would need to be tightened to not slip under the weight of the camera and/or if I put my camera bag on the hook.
The bag is snug enough even without adding the spike feed, but after mounting them, it just doesn't fit anymore.

Manfrotto Befree GT Travel Carbon Fiber.text: It was getting to be not enjoyable hiking with a heavy aluminum tripod. This one is much lighter and hiking photo adventures are now a pleasure again.

Reasonably light for the cost and easily holds my gear (Nikon D850 with 24-70 and 70-200 f2.8). ... Used it in the canyons in Utah. The tripod is more stable than I expected and though there is some plastic (the center column lock) the tripod feels robust.
if you over pullout the leg by accident, the shims inside of the tubes which are used to lock the legs could be missing, B & H does't provide this part replacement particularly for this model
Very sturdy and stable even in windy conditions. I like how you can invert the center post to get lower shots. It is a bit heavy though so keep that in mind.

Gitzo Traveler Series 1 GT1545T.text: I've had my 1545T (actually, the 100 year Anniversary Edition version) for 5+ years. It's been on 2 Japan birding trips and numerous U.S. trips. Great little tripod. Works well with EOS R5 and 100-500L lens
I will use the GT1545T for travel and multi day hiking when I want to travel light but don't want to compromise on height/stability
the 1545T has a small plastic key that prevents the column from rotating. The key can fall out too easily and can take a while to replace.
At full height its adequale in calm conditions or with smaller lenses.

JOBY GorillaPod 5K Kit.text: On assignment in remote Kenya, a leg popped off this brand new product and couldn't be put back on. This was only the third use.
Used lightly for 7 years but the rubber rings on the leg spheres are disintegrating and getting sticky
Purchased this as a replacement for a Joby I lost while hiking. Tripod is well made and holds my DSLR great.
Holds my Cannon R5 with the battery grip without issue

Manfrotto PIXI EVO 2-Section Mini Tripod.text: I got this mini tripod for a hiking trip in Arizona. It worked like a charm. Light and easy to pack, didn't even notice I had it until I needed it.

it's not quite stable enough with my Nikon Z6ii, battery grip, 105mm macro lens, and ring light attached to it. ... The legs seem to be fine but the ball head connection post seems to be what is flexing under the weight of my setup.
this tripod can't handle a tiny sony Zev 10 wich is 290 grams.
A wireless shutter controller is absolutely necessary to avoid tripod movement. If the camera is touched, the images shakes.
